correctness.rationale: Fresh reconstruction confirms the mathematical correction. A stable linear SDE with an additive compensated-Poisson term has a nonlocal jump generator and stationary Lévy stochastic convolution. For a scalar projection \(v^T Y\), the fourth cumulant is \(\int_0^\infty\!\int (v^\top e^{As}h(u))^4\,\nu(du)\,ds\); a nonzero value rules out a Gaussian law. Independently recomputing the package witness gives R~=26.6251093071, I*=3.3469399491, S*=0.5432290275, V*=0.5435059597, drift eigenvalues about −2.59513, −9.20189, −8.53162, and \(\kappa_4(e_1^\top Y_\infty)=2.22362604\times10^{-6}>0\). The true log-jump variance rate \(\log(1.1)^2=0.00908403037\) differs from 2(0.1−ln 1.1)=0.00937964039. Thus the displayed local Gaussian equation cannot be the exact stationary forward equation of the printed jump process.

value.rationale: The distinction between a genuine jump generator and a local diffusion equation is substantive: it changes the exact stationary law and already changes the covariance for an explicit admissible source parameter set. The correction identifies the Brownian-only exact boundary and the nonlocal term required for any exact jump-density calculation. This is more than a cosmetic notation issue, even though the source uses approximation language in places.

limitations: Corrects exactness of the linearized density statement, not the nonlinear stationary law.
Does not rule out a separately justified diffusion approximation with an explicit scaling/error bound.
